blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Recruitment is more than posting a job and reading CVs. It is a structured process — and every step affects the final result. It usually starts with a clear job description. Then comes sourcing: where will we look for candidates? LinkedIn, referrals, headhunters, internal mobility.

Next comes the screening — a short call to check the basics. After that, one or two rounds of interviews, perhaps a technical test, and finally the offer. Each stage exists for a reason, and skipping one rarely saves time in the end.

A professional recruiter keeps the candidate informed at every stage. Even a rejected candidate should leave the process with respect for the company — because today they are candidates, and tomorrow they might be clients, partners or brand ambassadors.

items.q: According to the text, what does recruitment start with?
items.why: "It usually starts with a clear job description."

items.q: What is the purpose of the screening stage?
options: To check the basics with a short call
items.why: "the screening — a short call to check the basics."

items.q: Which sources of candidates are mentioned in the text?
options: Job boards and print adverts only
LinkedIn, referrals, headhunters and internal mobility
items.why: "LinkedIn, referrals, headhunters, internal mobility."

items.q: The author suggests that a rejected candidate should be treated well because…
options: they may become a client, partner or brand ambassador later
they will reapply for the same role
items.why: Inferência: "tomorrow they might be clients, partners or brand ambassadors" — o cuidado tem valor de negócio.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: Candidates deserve to be kept informed.
Skipping a stage usually saves time overall.
Every step of the process affects the result.
items.why: Inferência: o texto defende que cada etapa existe por um motivo — pular etapas raramente economiza tempo.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Oliver treinando os novos recrutadores. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Welcome, everyone. Over the next hour I'll walk you through how we run recruitment here at Czarnikow — from the first briefing with the hiring manager, right through to the offer.

The mistake I made early in my career was rushing to post the advert. Don't. You should sit down with the manager first and agree exactly what the role needs. If the brief is vague, every stage after it will be vague too.

Once the pipeline is open, keep it moving. A candidate who waits ten days for feedback assumes we're not interested — and the good ones have other offers. So you must reply quickly, even when the answer is no. And always confirm salary expectations on the very first screening call. There's no point running someone through three interviews if the number was never going to work.

One last thing. Every candidate remembers how we treated them. Be honest, be fast, and never leave anyone guessing.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: What does Oliver's training cover?
options: The recruitment process from briefing to offer
items.why: "from the first briefing with the hiring manager, right through to the offer."

items.q: What mistake does Oliver say he made early in his career?
options: He rushed to post the advert
He offered too high a salary
items.why: "The mistake I made early in my career was rushing to post the advert."

items.q: When should recruiters confirm salary expectations?
options: On the very first screening call
items.why: "always confirm salary expectations on the very first screening call."

items.q: Why does Oliver insist on replying quickly, even to say no?
options: Because the manager reviews every reply
Because the law sets a deadline
Because slow feedback loses good candidates who have other offers
items.why: Inferência: "the good ones have other offers" — a demora custa os melhores candidatos.

items.q: What is Oliver's main message about candidate treatment?
options: Salary is the only thing candidates care about
How you treat every candidate is remembered, so be honest and fast
Feedback should be avoided to save time
items.why: Inferência: "Every candidate remembers how we treated them. Be honest, be fast."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We opened the sourcing phase on Monday and had twelve names by Friday." Sourcing is…
items.why: Sourcing = prospecção: buscar e atrair candidatos.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Half of our best hires came from a ___ — someone already on the team recommended them."
items.why: Referral = indicação: um candidato recomendado por alguém de dentro.

items.q: "After the screening we had a shortlist of three." A shortlist is…
options: the small final group selected to move forward
items.why: Shortlist = lista final: o grupo reduzido que segue no processo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "She accepted our offer, then her current employer made a ___ to keep her."
items.why: Counter-offer = contraproposta: a oferta do empregador atual para reter o candidato.

items.q: Candidate experience is best described as…
options: how a candidate perceives the whole recruitment process
how many years a candidate has worked
items.why: Candidate experience = experiência do candidato: como ele percebe o processo do início ao fim.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em processos de recrutamento. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The hiring manager still has to sign off on the offer." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We'll roll out the new screening template across all regions next quarter." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Two candidates dropped out before the final round." They…
options: left the process on their own
items.why: Drop out = sair, abandonar o processo por conta própria.

items.q: "Please follow up with the shortlist by Friday." To follow up means to…
options: make contact again to continue the process
items.why: Follow up = dar seguimento, retomar o contato.

items.q: "He turned down our offer and stayed where he was." To turn down means to…
items.why: Turn down = recusar, rejeitar (uma oferta).
